rows: When did tournaments begin?
~11th c. France; Geoffrey de Preuilly credited
What was the melee?
Mass team combat with actual weapons; ransoms the economic incentive
What was the tilt barrier?
Separator wall introduced ~13th c. to prevent horse collisions
How did William Marshal use tournaments?
As professional career -- ~500 captures, ransom income, rose from nothing to regent
Why was the longbow so effective?
Rate of fire (10-12/min); trained Welsh/English yeomen; massed volley tactics
What ended the longbow?
Matchlock firearm (~1590-1600): less training time, better armor penetration
What was Shrove Tuesday football?
Parish vs parish folk game, hundreds of players, minimal rules
When were blood sports banned in England?
1835 (Cruelty to Animals Act) -- bear, bull-baiting
Is Calcio Storico still played?
Yes -- Florence, June, four historical quarters, extremely violent
What was falconry?
Prestige aristocratic sport; Frederick II wrote systematic treatise ~1244
